results.title: Savannah's Great Dane wins Chinese tariff battle - The Current
results.content: After the ITC determined that the U.S. trailer manufacturers have been materially injured by imports, the Commerce Department last week instructed customs authorities to add duties ranging from 82.3% to 128.7% for trailers from China and 1.9% to 1.95% for trailers from Mexico. [...] U.S. customs officials are poised to levy new duties on semitruck trailers made in China and Mexico after a yearlong legal battle fought by Savannah’s Great Dane LLC and two other American manufacturers of this essential component of the trucking industry. [...] Those three companies estimate that about 40% of the U.S. market for van trailers is supplied by China, Mexico and Canada combined. Import data suggests that foreign suppliers, mainly Chinese, have boosted their sales in America from about 48,000 van trailers annually between 2015-2017 to 80,600 between 2022 and 2024.

results.content: But it’s not just about higher prices. Tariffs also have the potential to disrupt supply chains. With tariffs on imported goods, particularly raw materials and components sourced from other countries, manufacturers may face delays or shortages in receiving the parts they need to complete their production. For example, steel from overseas might take longer to arrive due to customs delays or logistical bottlenecks, slowing down production schedules and delaying delivery times for consumers.
